steps: New memories are made, and the girl, troubled by her past, finds her rock.
In the afternoon, we finish delivering the rest of the letters one by one, then take a break on a bench by the roadside near Post Haste.
I wasn't sure what kind of snacks you like, so I picked up a bit of everything.
Sorry about today. So many unexpected things came up.
Not at all. You were amazing, Freesia.
When you two said you were going to duel, I was seriously worried.
Dueling was the easiest solution given the situation.
He was the one who challenged me, I just accepted.
By the way, Aoi and Auntie Helen also mentioned "duels"—what exactly are they?
Aoi skipped class to hang out with her sister, and I happened to catch them.
They refused to go back to class, so I challenged them to a "Marble Champion Showdown" duel.
Yes. I won fair and square and they promised me they'd never skip class again.
And I promised them that as long as they behaved, we could hang out and play it again.
So that's why she was so keen on having another duel with you... ==W==What about the duel Auntie Helen mentioned?
That was with a giant boar.
It probably ran out from the nearby forest and wandered into Auntie Helen's yard.
I was hoping to talk things out with it, but it refused to listen to reason.
So I challenged it to a duel. It lost and I dragged it back into the forest.
I can't believe you took down a wild boar so easily...
No wonder everyone's so grateful. You're such a great help to them.
When Aoi mentioned the duel earlier, you looked so nervous. I thought it was some kind of big secret.
… S-sorry, I didn't mean to hide it from you.
I was worried that hearing about the duel might make you think poorly of me ...==W== or Post Haste.
Most people, when they first hear about it, think it's some kind of barbaric practice.
I've heard a bit about the old "Trial by Dueling" tradition myself. Settling things like that is actually pretty effective.
Besides, you don't duel for selfish purposes. You do it to help people.
Still, it was terribly improper of me to duel in front of you.
When I'm in a duel... I've been told… I can get pretty scary.
Even if I said I wouldn't think that, Freesia would probably just assume I was trying to make her feel better.
...==W== Ah, there's only one piece of snack left.
I'll leave this one for you, Freesia.
No... Please, Boss, you should be the one to enjoy it.
A divergence of opinions... ==W==We need a way to settle this.
The winner gets to decide who can have the final piece of snack.
The duel is in the form of a marble game, with both sides in full agreement.
Let me see how good you are, Freesia.
Very well, Boss. I'm going to give it my best shot.
Just a drizzle. It should stop soon.
Do you want to go back first and duel after the rain?
No, thank you.==W== A duel in the rain is more exciting.
Come, Boss. This is our final showdown.
Yup. I won't go easy on you.
Then I will do the countdown.
My last shot! Here it comes!
The marble streaks low and fast, carving a perfect arc as it races straight toward its target.
Thank you for the challenge. Say, you don't look that different when you are dueling, Freesia.
Just a little more serious than usual.
Boss, I know what you're trying to do. You didn't have to.
It was never about winning the duel for you, was it?
You saw right through it, huh?
But I swear, I never underestimated you. I gave it everything I had.
Same here. It was an honor to duel with you.
Since the decision is mine to make, I want you to have the last piece of snack.
And as agreed, I shall accept it.
As Freesia heads upstairs to change, I sit down on the living room sofa by myself.
Brr, I'm freezing soaked through. Guess I'll just have to wait for my clothes to dry.
Kinda sleepy from running around all day...
Boss,==W== please wake up.==W== I brought you some dry clothes.==W== You should change out of those wet ones.
With this weather,==W== you could easily catch a cold if you stay in soaked clothes.
Oh, it's fine... Don't worry about me
I really appreciate all your help today.==W== I'd feel terrible==W== if you were to fall ill because of me.==W==
I didn't really do much … honestly
You were always there for me today,==W== delivering letters, supporting my duel,==W== and playing marbles with you.
Still...==W== I honestly didn't expect you ==W==to dive in to those "childish games" quite so enthusiastically. ==W==You were really good at them, too!==W==
If anything, I should be the one thanking you
Aw, thanks.==W== But ... it looks like the rain is picking up, doesn't it?
The truth is...==W== I don't have very fond memories of rainy days. ==W==Just the sound of it seems to weigh on my heart.==W==
Does the rain still bother you?

Not anymore,==W== because I've made a new memory.==W== Starting tomorrow,==W== when it rains again,==W== the first thing I'll think of ...==W== is this night with you—==W==steady and unshakable==W== in my heart.
If I can do that, who knows? ==W==I might learn to even like rainy days. ==W==So, again... ==W==Thank you.
Oh my. ==W==Your hair's all damp. ==W====W==Stay still, please, and let me dry it for you.
The rain didn't stop that night.==B== It lashed and the wind howled outside, but Post Haste stood firm, offering warmth and shelter for Freesia and me.
